title: Aboriginal Land Rights and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2013
portfolio: Families, Housing, Community Services and Indigenous Affairs

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would enable Aboriginal land grants around Jabiru and at Patta, while changing leasing and town planning rules within Commonwealth reserves.
It would add Jabiru and two adjacent land portions for grant to the Kakadu Aboriginal Land Trust, subject to arrangements for leasing them back.
The Jabiru land would remain within a Commonwealth reserve, and environmental amendments would address protection of Kakadu's world heritage, natural and cultural values.
changes: A further Patta land parcel would become eligible for grant to the relevant Aboriginal Land Trust.
The Minister could establish Aboriginal Land Trusts to hold land beyond Crown land.
The Minister would have to consult the Northern Territory Government and relevant Land Council before specifying Jabiru town land.
The legislation would take effect on the day after Royal Assent.
summary.affected: The Kakadu Aboriginal Land Trust, the Aboriginal Land Trust receiving the Patta parcel, Land Councils, the Northern Territory and the Director of National Parks are affected.

speeches.speaker: Anne McEwen
speeches.brief: The Selection of Bills Committee presented its fourth report of 2013, recommending 18 bills be referred to various Senate committees for inquiry and report by specific dates, and that certain other bills not be referred.

speeches.speaker: Kevin Andrews
speeches.brief: Introduced the Aboriginal Land Rights and Other Legislation Amendment Bill, which would add Jabiru, two nearby parcels and land near Tennant Creek to schedule 1 for inalienable Aboriginal freehold title subject to a 99-year lease back arrangement.

speeches.speaker: Nigel Scullion
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Aboriginal Land Rights and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2013, noting that the Northern Territory government, Northern Land Council, and local Aboriginal land trust back the scheduling of three land parcels, and that ERA seeks to avoid a painful native title negotiation. The speaker commended the parties for agreeing to reschedule the township of Jabiru under the act, despite criticism from others.
